title: 390. The psychology of serial monogamy & relationship hopping

sentences.en: Hello, everybody.
sentences.zh: 大家好。

sentences.en: I'm Gemma Spake, and welcome back to The Psychology of Your 20s, the podcast where we talk through the biggest changes, moments, and transitions of our 20s,
sentences.zh: 我是 Gemma Spake，欢迎回到《二十岁的心理学》，这是一档探讨我们二十岁时所经历的最大变化、时刻和转折点的播客，

sentences.en: and what they mean for our psychology.
sentences.zh: 以及它们对我们心理意味着什么。

sentences.en: Hello, everybody.
sentences.zh: 大家好。

sentences.en: Welcome back to the show.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到节目。

sentences.en: Welcome back to the podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到播客。

sentences.en: It is so great to have you here back for another episode.
sentences.zh: 很高兴你能回来收听新的一期节目。

sentences.en: I am very excited for this episode because I think it's something that a lot of us are going to find relevant and very revealing.
sentences.zh: 我对这一期非常兴奋，因为我认为它与我们许多人息息相关，而且非常具有启发性。

sentences.en: Today, we are talking about serial monogamy or relationship hopping.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们要讨论的是连续单身主义或“恋爱跳跃”。

sentences.en: I think it is safe to say we have all had, we all know that one person, that one friend who seemingly cannot stay single for any period of time, who's always in a relationship.
sentences.zh: 我想可以肯定地说，我们都认识那样一个人，那个似乎无法忍受哪怕片刻单身、总是处于恋爱关系中的朋友。

sentences.en: We all have encountered that person in our dating lives who maybe wants something suspiciously fast despite having just gone through a breakup.
sentences.zh: 在我们的约会生活中，我们都遇到过那样的人，他们可能在刚经历分手后，就迫不及待地想要开始下一段关系。

sentences.en: Somebody who really seems to be hell-bent on finding a relationship after only just ending one very, very previously, very shortly before.
sentences.zh: 有些人似乎铁了心要在结束一段关系后，在极短的时间内立刻寻找下一段。

sentences.en: Maybe you are that person.
sentences.zh: 也许你就是那样的人。

sentences.en: This is what we're talking about today, relationship hopping.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们今天要讨论的话题：恋爱跳跃。

sentences.en: This situation, phenomena, where somebody jumps quickly from relationship to relationship without really leaving any time for emotional processing,
sentences.zh: 这种情况，这种现象，指的是某人迅速地从一段关系跳到另一段关系，而没有留出任何时间进行情感处理、

sentences.en: for healing, for self-reflection.
sentences.zh: 疗愈或自我反思。

sentences.en: It's not simply going on a few dates after a bad breakup or meeting a new person kind of serendipitously after a bad breakup.
sentences.zh: 这不仅仅是在糟糕的分手后去约会几次，或者在分手后偶然遇到一个新人。

sentences.en: We've all done it.
sentences.zh: 我们都经历过。

sentences.en: We've all, I think, had those moments where, well, maybe not all of us, but I think it's pretty normal to sometimes have those moments where a relationship ends
sentences.zh: 我想我们都有过这样的时刻——好吧，也许不是我们所有人，但我认为有时在一段关系结束后，

sentences.en: and you happen to find somebody really amazing pretty soon after.
sentences.zh: 很快就遇到一个非常棒的人，这其实很正常。

sentences.en: What we are talking about instead is this pattern of quickly needing
sentences.zh: 我们今天要讨论的是那种需要迅速让

sentences.en: emotionally significant relationships to follow each other.
sentences.zh: 情感上重要的关系接踵而至的模式。

sentences.en: Very much needing exclusivity, needing a partner in your life, often having very little space in between the people you date.
sentences.zh: 非常需要排他性，需要生活中有一个伴侣，而且在约会对象之间几乎没有留出任何空档。

sentences.en: Before we let our minds assume that this is a personality flaw, I have got to remind you, this isn't necessarily bad.
sentences.zh: 在我们认定这是一种性格缺陷之前，我必须提醒你，这并不一定就是坏事。

sentences.en: Like I said, some people genuinely thrive in partnership, they date intentionally, perhaps for religious or personal reasons, and that's fine.
sentences.zh: 就像我说的，有些人确实在伴侣关系中成长得更好，他们是有意地去约会，也许是出于宗教或个人原因，这没问题。

sentences.en: But the question is, what do you lose when you do that, if anything?
sentences.zh: 但问题是，当你这样做时，你失去了什么（如果有的话）？

sentences.en: And why do some people feel almost unable to be single, whereas other people avoid relationships entirely?
sentences.zh: 为什么有些人几乎无法忍受单身，而另一些人却完全回避恋爱？

sentences.en: What is that human difference that makes people go either of those ways?
sentences.zh: 是什么样的人性差异导致人们走向这两个极端？

sentences.en: So let's start with, I guess some basics, not so much a definition, but some parameters around what makes somebody a serial monogamiSt.
sentences.zh: 所以，让我们从一些基础知识开始，与其说是定义，不如说是关于什么样的人属于“连续单身主义者”的一些参数。

sentences.en: There is no definition.
sentences.zh: 目前还没有标准的定义。

sentences.en: I personally think you could label yourself or somebody you know as a serial monogamist when they consistently leave less than three months between significant relationships,
sentences.zh: 我个人认为，当一个人在两段重要关系之间持续留出的空档少于三个月时，你就可以给他们或你认识的人贴上“连续单身主义者”的标签，

sentences.en: or they consistently leave less than three months between leaving a relationship and actively seeking out another committed relationship.
sentences.zh: 或者他们从结束一段关系到积极寻求另一段承诺关系之间，持续留出的空档少于三个月。

sentences.en: This is not just a one-off, it's not just a long time coming after a breakup, and it's not just rebound relationships after.
sentences.zh: 这不仅仅是一次偶然，不是分手后很久才开始，也不是分手后的反弹式恋爱。

sentences.en: This is sought-out commitment.
sentences.zh: 这是主动寻求的承诺。

sentences.en: A rebound relationship, you know, a rebound relationship is usually just a single event, and I think it's usually just about distraction, right?
sentences.zh: 反弹式恋爱，你知道的，通常只是一个单一事件，我认为它通常只是为了分散注意力，对吧？

sentences.en: It's partly about soothing, it's partly about proving you're desirable, it's partly about feeling like you need to do the things that single people do after being in a relationship
sentences.zh: 它部分是为了自我安慰，部分是为了证明自己有吸引力，部分是因为觉得在经历了一段时间的恋爱后，

sentences.en: for a while.
sentences.zh: 需要做单身人士该做的事情。

sentences.en: Sometimes it's just about a new connection, but you kind of know with rebound relationships, they're not going to laSt.
sentences.zh: 有时它只是关于一段新的连接，但你心里清楚，反弹式恋爱是不会长久的。

sentences.en: Relationship hopping, though, is seeking relationships that will be something meaningful for you, and it's this state, emotional state, where being single
sentences.zh: 然而，“恋爱跳跃”是寻求那些对你有意义的关系，这是一种情感状态，在这种状态下，单身

sentences.en: is like completely intolerable, and you really do require a relationship for emotional stability, a sense of emotional and self-centeredness, not self-centeredness
sentences.zh: 是完全无法忍受的，你确实需要一段关系来获得情感稳定，获得一种情感和自我中心感——不是那种自私的自我中心，

sentences.en: in like the egotistical way, but like self-stability in a way,
sentences.zh: 而是指一种自我稳定感，

sentences.en: and you don't know who you are or what to do without it.
sentences.zh: 如果没有它，你就不知道自己是谁，也不知道该做什么。

sentences.en: Again, this isn't some moral flaw or something that you should be ashamed of, but you should be aware of it because maybe it is causing you to make rash dating
sentences.zh: 再说一次，这并不是什么道德缺陷，也不应该为此感到羞耻，但你应该意识到这一点，因为它可能导致你做出草率的约会

sentences.en: or relationship decisions you otherwise wouldn't, and I honestly think that most of the time, at its minimum, at its lowest, it is causing you to miss out on the deep,
sentences.zh: 或恋爱决定，而这些决定在平时你可能不会做。我真心认为，大多数时候，至少在最低程度上，它让你错失了

sentences.en: deep self-discovery that you get from being alone for a while, and the privilege that you get from being single,
sentences.zh: 通过独处一段时间所获得的深刻的自我发现，以及单身所带来的特权，

sentences.en: especially during your 20s.
sentences.zh: 尤其是在你二十多岁的时候。

sentences.en: So a big question you may be asking is, again, why am I like this?
sentences.zh: 所以，你可能想问的一个大问题是：为什么我会这样？

sentences.en: Why are some people like this?
sentences.zh: 为什么有些人会这样？

sentences.en: This is where attachment theory comes in, but not as you know it, without giving you like the whole rundown of like all the different attachment styles because I feel like
sentences.zh: 这就是依恋理论发挥作用的地方，但不是你所熟知的那种，我不会给你列举所有不同的依恋类型，因为我觉得

sentences.en: that's been done to death.
sentences.zh: 那已经被讲烂了。

sentences.en: Let me just say this.
sentences.zh: 我只想说这一点。

sentences.en: Attachment is essentially just your unique blueprint for how you respond to closeness, how you respond to love, how you respond to uncertainty, and how you respond
sentences.zh: 依恋本质上就是你独特的蓝图，决定了你如何回应亲密关系，如何回应爱，如何回应不确定性，以及如何回应

sentences.en: to emotional threats inside and outside of relationships.
sentences.zh: 关系内外的各种情感威胁。

sentences.en: People with anxious attachment styles are often more likely to be serial monogamous.
sentences.zh: 焦虑型依恋的人通常更有可能成为连续单身主义者。

sentences.en: We know that's probably because they struggle, they struggle with the fear of abandonment, they struggle with the idea that somebody could leave them, so having a label
sentences.zh: 我们知道这可能是因为他们挣扎，他们害怕被抛弃，他们挣扎于“有人可能会离开他们”的想法，所以拥有一个标签

sentences.en: is really comforting.
sentences.zh: 会让人感到非常安慰。

sentences.en: But another influential idea coming from these researchers in the 80s, their names were Cassidy and Kobach, basically what they thought was that anxious attached people,
sentences.zh: 但 80 年代的两位研究人员 Cassidy 和 Kobach 提出了另一个有影响力的观点，他们认为焦虑型依恋的人，

sentences.en: they often use hyper-activating strategies to self-soothe, whereas avoidant people use under-activating strategies to self-soothe.
sentences.zh: 通常使用“过度激活策略”来自我安抚，而回避型的人则使用“低激活策略”来自我安抚。

sentences.en: So essentially, people who are anxious make themselves feel better by turning up the volume and turning up the intensity of a relationship.
sentences.zh: 所以本质上，焦虑的人通过调高音量和增加关系的强度来让自己感觉好受些。

sentences.en: Reassurance seeking, forcing urgency, forcing proximity, putting more focus on the relationship as a solution to their discomfort, whereas people who are avoidant
sentences.zh: 寻求保证、强迫紧迫感、强迫亲近、将更多注意力放在关系上作为解决不适的方案；而回避型的人

sentences.en: want to turn all of that down.
sentences.zh: 则想要调低所有这些。

sentences.en: Seeking proximity, seeking deep intimacy,
sentences.zh: 寻求亲近，寻求深度亲密，

sentences.en: sometimes with whoever comes through the door first, it is a self-regulating strategy.
sentences.zh: 有时不管先遇到谁，这都是一种自我调节策略。

sentences.en: Because when we feel dangerous or we feel uncertain about the future, when we feel uncertain about whether we'll find love again, whether we'll be lonely, whether we'll be,
sentences.zh: 因为当我们感到危险或对未来感到不确定时，当我们不确定是否还能再次找到爱，是否会孤独，是否会，

sentences.en: whether we'll find peace, it's very easy to put off thinking those things if you have somebody in your life you can say, oh, look at this,
sentences.zh: 是否会找到平静时，如果你生命中有个人，你可以说“哦，看，

sentences.en: I've got this person, this person who cares about me, I must be doing something right.
sentences.zh: 我有这个人，这个关心我的人，我一定做对了什么”，那么不去思考那些问题就变得非常容易。

sentences.en: That is why some people feel safest when they have a partner because it feels like something in their life is going right.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么有些人拥有伴侣时感到最安全，因为这让他们觉得生活中有事情正在步入正轨。

sentences.en: It feels like they're doing something that society approves of.
sentences.zh: 这让他们觉得自己在做社会认可的事情。

sentences.en: It feels like and it represents to them that they have a place to go home to.
sentences.zh: 这让他们觉得，并且代表了他们有一个可以回到的地方。

sentences.en: They have somebody who cares about them and they have been chosen.
sentences.zh: 他们有人关心，并且他们被选择了。

sentences.en: So there's this whole mix of things bubbling up, anxiety, self-esteem, self-worth, nervous system regulation, attachment.
sentences.zh: 所以这里有一堆东西在冒泡：焦虑、自尊、自我价值、神经系统调节、依恋。

sentences.en: The irony of relationship hopping though is that
sentences.zh: 然而，“恋爱跳跃”的讽刺之处在于，

sentences.en: I think ironically we think people who are in relationships must be secure and those who are out of them must be, have something wrong with their attachment style
sentences.zh: 我认为讽刺的是，我们认为处于恋爱关系中的人一定很安全，而那些单身的人一定在依恋类型上出了问题，

sentences.en: but people who are always in relationships are sometimes the most anxious and disorganized people internally.
sentences.zh: 但那些总是处于恋爱关系中的人，有时内心却是最焦虑、最混乱的。

sentences.en: Being partnered doesn't automatically equal emotional safety or emotional maturity.
sentences.zh: 拥有伴侣并不自动等同于情感安全或情感成熟。

sentences.en: It can sometimes just be that we have this coping strategy of seeking emotional closeness with others that means you know from the outside it always seems like
sentences.zh: 有时这可能只是因为我们有一种寻求与他人情感亲近的应对策略，这意味着从外表看，一切似乎

sentences.en: everything's going well.
sentences.zh: 都进展顺利。

sentences.en: It always seems like we've got somebody who cares about us and loves us and you know we must be we must be the shit we must be pretty great.
sentences.zh: 看起来我们总是有个关心我们、爱我们的人，你知道，我们一定很棒，我们一定很了不起。

sentences.en: But the thing is is that those relationships and I'm not going to speak for your experiences just from what I've seen those relationships are often quite shallow
sentences.zh: 但问题是，那些关系——我不是在说你的经历，只是根据我所看到的——那些关系往往相当肤浅，

sentences.en: because real vulnerability and real connection like we know this you know this it takes time and it takes difficult things to bond to bond people together.
sentences.zh: 因为真正的脆弱和真正的连接——我们知道这一点，你也知道——需要时间，也需要经历困难的事情才能将人们紧密联系在一起。

sentences.en: It's awkward.
sentences.zh: 这很尴尬。

sentences.en: Real vulnerability is actually really awkward because it involves risk.
sentences.zh: 真正的脆弱实际上非常尴尬，因为它涉及风险。

sentences.en: It involves the risk of reaching out to somebody and then rejecting you.
sentences.zh: 它涉及向某人敞开心扉却被拒绝的风险。

sentences.en: It involves the risk of being chosen and being safe and being loved and then maybe somebody turning around and not feeling those same things towards you and you know just kind of
sentences.zh: 它涉及被选择、感到安全和被爱，然后可能有人转过身来，对你没有同样的感受，你知道，仅仅是

sentences.en: knowing that knowing that's a possibility and still trusting them especially in those early stages especially when you're first getting to know somebody.
sentences.zh: 知道这是一种可能性，却依然信任他们，尤其是在早期阶段，尤其是在你刚开始了解某人的时候。

sentences.en: Now if you are somebody who is very anxious and has a deep rooted fear of rejection or abandonment those early those early days those early stages of risk and vulnerability
sentences.zh: 现在，如果你是一个非常焦虑、内心深处害怕被拒绝或抛弃的人，那些早期的、那些充满风险和脆弱的早期阶段，

sentences.en: and uncertainty that can be unbearable.
sentences.zh: 以及不确定性，那可能是无法忍受的。

sentences.en: It can be unbearable to like your self-esteem and to your sense of emotional safety so instead you chase that artificial closeness.
sentences.zh: 这对你的自尊和情感安全感来说可能是无法忍受的，所以你转而追求那种人为的亲近。

sentences.en: You chase the closeness that is created by structure and created by proximity and created by a label and created by fast commitment and fast enmeshment and fast emotional intimacy
sentences.zh: 你追求那种由结构、亲近感、标签、快速承诺、快速纠缠和快速情感亲密所创造的亲近感，

sentences.en: rather than just sometimes letting things happen naturally and it's not manipulative this isn't a character flaw it's self-protection it's a logic of thinking
sentences.zh: 而不是顺其自然。这并不是操纵，也不是性格缺陷，这是一种自我保护，是一种逻辑思维：

sentences.en: if I make this official really quickly if I lock this person down fast
sentences.zh: 如果我能很快让关系正式化，如果我能迅速锁定这个人，

sentences.en: I'll be safe if you know who cares if I just met this person three weeks ago a week ago if they're my partner and they have that label then they can't they can't leave me
sentences.zh: 我就安全了。谁在乎我是否三周前、一周前才认识这个人？如果他们是我的伴侣，有那个标签，那么他们就不能，他们就不能离开我。

sentences.en: that's one more barrier to them walking out on me like the last person did or this relationship crumbling like the last one did really I think sometimes relationship hopping
sentences.zh: 那是他们像上一个人那样抛弃我，或者这段关系像上一段那样崩溃的又一道屏障。真的，我认为有时“恋爱跳跃”

sentences.en: is really just a way of avoiding the grief associated with past hurt you know think about what happens after a breakup you're going to feel something you have to feel something
sentences.zh: 真的只是为了避免与过去的伤害相关的悲伤。你知道，想想分手后会发生什么，你会感觉到一些东西，你必须感觉到一些东西：

sentences.en: pain betrayal longing
sentences.zh: 痛苦、背叛、渴望、

sentences.en: anger and there's often this quiet period that really demands we sit with ourselves and let ourselves be confronted with really big emotional questions that kind of suck to answer
sentences.zh: 愤怒。而且通常会有一段安静的时期，要求我们与自己独处，让我们面对那些很难回答的重大情感问题，

sentences.en: but questions like who am I outside of outside of this relationship what do I do with my evenings now why didn't this work out what happens if I don't find somebody better
sentences.zh: 比如：在这段关系之外我是谁？我现在晚上该做什么？为什么这段关系没能成功？如果我找不到更好的人怎么办？

sentences.en: what happens if I don't find somebody period
sentences.zh: 如果我根本找不到人怎么办？

sentences.en: and for you know a period of time we don't know the answer
sentences.zh: 有一段时间，我们不知道答案。

sentences.en: we don't know who we are outside of a relationship we don't know for certain if we're going to be okay if we're going to find somebody we like as much as that last person
sentences.zh: 我们不知道在一段关系之外我们是谁，我们不确定如果我们要好起来，如果我们要找到像上一个人那样让我们喜欢的人，我们是否能做到。
